The test image shows a whole-plant field view with widespread plant collapse/wilting across many rows. Plants are green but severely prostrated/wilted. This narrows to whole_plant candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Late_Blight, Verticillium_Wilt.

The sudden widespread collapse pattern across the whole field strongly suggests a wilt disease. I'll use my one reference view on Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

The reference shows Southern_Bacterial_Wilt with drooping leaves on a standing plant. The test image is more extreme — entire field of plants completely prostrated/collapsed to the ground while still green. This is classic rapid vascular wilt at the field scale.

The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference doesn't quite match the severity. The test image shows complete plant collapse across the whole field, which is the hallmark of **Bacterial_Wilt** (Ralstonia solanacearum) causing sudden, rapid wilt — plants go from healthy to completely collapsed while remaining green, across the entire field simultaneously.

Southern_Bacterial_Wilt is similar but the reference image showed a single plant drooping, not field-wide prostration. The complete collapse while maintaining green color is consistent with rapid vascular occlusion from bacterial wilt."}
